messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager: potential cross-tenant routing detected in Dedicated pool dp-4321. Rule triggered: opaque-prefix-detection. Observed prefix injected into dataplane that does not match tenant allocation. Auto-tags: customer-impact-possible, needs-oncall
Samir P: Oncall here — acknowledged. What’s the initial scope? Which tenants/pools?
Elaine H: seeing the alert. dp-4321 is a shared-dedicated pool used by a handful of enterprise private deployments (VPCs). Please do not post PII.
Mike C: quick check — running pool-affinity dump now.
Mike C: ```bash
$ infractl pool-affinity --pool dp-4321 --json
{
  "nodes": [
    {"node": "node-12", "tenant": "cust-echelon", "tenant_id": "t-842"},
    {"node": "node-13", "tenant": "cust-acme", "tenant_id": "t-101"}
  ],
  "config": {"vpc_id": "vpc-007-eu", "region": "eu-west-1"}
}
```
Mike C: that output looks wrong — node-12 and node-13 should both be t-842 for dp-4321. Possible config drift or routing table leak.
Jia L: security — start forensic capture (pcap) on node-12 and node-13 and preserve kernel routing tables. We want flow logs + kv-prefix-audit.
Samir P: Agreed. Immediate mitigation: isolate the pool to stop further cross-tenant traffic. Options: (1) disable inter-pool routing flag; (2) drain affected nodes; (3) apply iptables to drop prefixes. Prefer quick stop-gap then controlled evacuation.
Elaine H: I’ll coordinate. Mike, can you do a quick iptables drop for the suspect prefix and kick off drain? Post exact commands here.
Mike C: applying drop now and starting drain.
Mike C: ```bash
# emergency block suspect prefix
sudo iptables -I FORWARD -d 100.64.12.0/22 -j DROP
# start evacuation
infractl drain --pool dp-4321 --nodes node-12,node-13 --mode evacuate --reason "suspected cross-tenant routing" --ticket 17401
```
InfraBot: Job infractl/evacuate-17401 submitted. ETA for drain completion: ~18m.
IncidentBot: Noting impacted customers potentially attached to nodes: cust-echelon (t-842) and cust-acme (t-101). Marking incident priority: P1-customer-impact.
Jia L: Forensic notes: capture /var/log/redwood/route-manager.log, kv-prefix snapshots, and network tap for 10m prior to alert. Also flag for potential in-memory KV cache contamination.
Samir P: Quick check — any evidence of token leaks or persisted data exfil?
Mike C: short answer: no tokens observed in logs so far. We’ve seen traffic where requests were routed to the wrong backend for short windows (seconds-minutes). Example from route-manager.log: ```
[2026-11-07T09:13:12Z] route-assignment: prefix=100.64.12.0/22 assigned_to=t-101 (expected t-842) src=controlplane cfg_ver=537
```
Mike C: That indicates control plane pushed an incorrect mapping. Could be a race during a config rollout.
Elaine H: I'm pausing all control-plane pool-affinity rollouts in eu-west-1. @infra-team please hold.
Jia L: Customer impact assessment: cust-echelon may have experienced misrouted inference requests to cust-acme's VPC for ~6 minutes. Need to notify cust-echelon CSE and Security. Recommend rotating any short-lived API keys surfaced and offering support.
Samir P: Agreed. Escalating to SRE lead and Security. Also open an incident ticket with forensics checklist and assign to eng-runtime for root cause.
Mike C: Collected artifacts: route-manager.log (last 24h), pool-affinity snapshots, kernel netstat snapshots, pcap (10m). Uploading to secure case bucket now.
InfraBot: Artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-17401/artifacts/ — access granted to incident-role only.
Elaine H: Mitigation status: iptables block in place, drain in progress (node-12 still terminating connections). Control-plane rollouts paused. No new misrouted requests observed after block.
Samir P: Next steps: 1) finish evacuation, 2) full mapping audit across dp-* pools for similar mismatches, 3) postmortem scheduled within 72h, 4) customer outreach draft (security + cs) for affected tenants.
Jia L: Also recommend temporary key rotations for tenants with sensitive workloads and an invite-only call with cust-echelon security team.
Mike C: Note for eng-runtime: check kernel-level race in route assignment reconciler; add assert to prevent assigning existing prefix to a different tenant without explicit unbind step.
Elaine H: I’ll take the incident lead for coordination. Assigning follow-ups: audit -> Mike C, forensics -> Jia L, runtime RC -> eng-runtime oncall.
Samir P: Marking this thread for post-incident follow-up. Will update status when drain completes and once customer notification goes out. :white_check_mark:
